articles.originalTitle: Momentous 61st Venice Biennale Ends With 2nd-Highest Visitor Turnout - Hyperallergic
articles.title: 61st Venice Biennale Concludes With High Visitor Turnout
articles.excerpt: Curated by the late Koyo Kouoh, the 61st Venice Biennale drew 714,015 visitors over its six-month run, marking the second-highest attendance in the event's history.
articles.content: The 61st Venice Biennale, curated by the late Koyo Kouoh, concluded on November 22 after a six-month run, reporting 714,015 visitors. Despite running three weeks shorter than previous editions to allow for the renovation of the Central Pavilion at the Giardini, the exhibition achieved the second-highest attendance in the event's history. The 2022 edition continues to hold the record with more than 800,000 visitors. Nearly 30,000 people attended the pre-opening events. Following Kouoh's death in May 2025, a team of collaborators comprising Rasha Salti, Marie Hélène Pereira, Gabe Beckhurst Feijoo, Siddhartha Mitter, and Rory Tsapayi carried out the exhibition. Featuring 109 international artists, many hailing from Africa and the Caribbean diasporas, the event included a record-high 100 participating countries. This high turnout follows peak visitor numbers at recent editions of the Venice Architecture Biennale and Venice International Film Festival, both organized under La Biennale di Venezia.

articles.originalTitle: inside ZHA’s royal theater in morocco, white curves meet crystalline caverns - Designboom
articles.title: Zaha Hadid Architects Completes Royal Theater in Morocco
articles.excerpt: Zaha Hadid Architects has revealed new photographs of the Théâtre Royal de Rabat, marking its first realized project in Africa.
articles.content: Zaha Hadid Architects has revealed the completed architecture of the Théâtre Royal de Rabat through new photographs, marking its first realized project in Africa. Originally announced in 2010, construction began in 2014, and the building received a ceremonial inauguration in October 2024. Its first public performance followed in April 2026. Situated between Rabat and Salé, the theater forms part of a cultural development program initiated by King Mohammed VI. Drawing from the tidal landscape of the Bouregreg River, the theater features sweeping white surfaces rising from the riverbank. The complex concrete structure is wrapped in molded glass-fiber-reinforced concrete panels. An open-air amphitheater with a capacity of 7,000 spectators extends eastward. Inside, a triple-height public foyer welcomes visitors with interwoven staircases. The 1,821-seat main auditorium features angular, crystalline surfaces inspired by traditional Moroccan muqarnas. These acoustic surfaces were developed alongside Arup New York. The complex also includes a 250-seat Studio Theatre for experimental productions.

articles.title: 2026 World Architecture Festival Winners Announced at Florida Gala Dinner
articles.excerpt: Prestige University in India has been named World Building of the Year at the 2026 World Architecture Festival in Florida. The event also announced the World Interior of the Year, Future Project of the Year, and various special category prizes.
articles.content: The Prestige University in Indore, India, designed by Sanjay Puri Architects, was declared World Building of the Year at the 2026 World Architecture Festival held at the Broward County Convention Center in Florida. The nineteenth edition of the festival concluded with a gala dinner announcing the ultimate accolades, including World Building of the Year, World Interior of the Year, and Future Project of the Year, alongside numerous special prizes. Situated on a 32-acre campus, the winning university complex houses administrative offices, an open-air auditorium, seminar halls, a library, and a cafeteria. The structure gradually steps up to form a multifunctional stage seating 9000 students. The architectural form draws inspiration from traditional Indian stepwells, while naturally lit internal courtyards minimize reliance on artificial lighting and air conditioning in a climate ranging from 30°C to 40°C. Evaluated by a super jury chaired by Professor Grace La of the Harvard Graduate School of Design, the festival also awarded World Interior of the Year to &Matcha Three Yards in the Philippines. The Future Project of the Year went to Coding Kelp by Terreform ONE in Canada. Additional category winners included projects spanning architectural color, landscape, sustainability, and regional design excellence.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: From Constantinople to Istanbul: Exhibition Explores Two Empires' History
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum released a large print guide for the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition, detailing the city's rich history, art, and architecture across Roman and Ottoman periods.
articles.content: In 324 CE, Roman emperor Constantine chose the ancient Greek city of Byzantion as a new capital, renaming it Nova Roma in 330 CE. The city soon became known as Constantinople, capital of the Byzantine Empire. Following the fall of the Byzantine capital in 1453, the city rose again as Istanbul, the new capital of the Ottoman Empire, remaining so until 1922. Located at the meeting point of Asia and Europe, the metropolis attracted merchants, artists, and pilgrims through its strategic sea routes. The exhibition examines the city's two distinct art and design traditions under Byzantine and Ottoman rule, featuring architecture, land walls, water-supply systems, and Christian relics. While Byzantine Constantinople featured central depictions of sacred figures in public spaces and churches, the Ottomans avoided such images, often utilizing calligraphy instead. Featuring objects from institutions such as the Istanbul Archaeological Museums and the Chester Beatty Library, the guide illuminates the multi-layered heritage of the historic metropolis.

articles.originalTitle: Russian strikes damage historic buildings in Kyiv and Odesa, including World Heritage sites - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Russian Strikes Damage Historic Buildings in Kyiv and Odesa
articles.excerpt: Multiple cultural heritage sites in Ukraine, including UNESCO-listed locations in Kyiv and Odesa, sustained damage during recent Russian attacks.
articles.content: Russian strikes on November 19 and 20 damaged multiple heritage sites in Ukraine, including the UNESCO-listed St. Michael's Golden-Domed Cathedral and Monastery complex, the frescoed St. Volodymyr's Cathedral in Kyiv, and 12 cultural heritage sites in Odesa. Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Tetyana Berezhna reported that the Volodymyr Cathedral sustained damage to structural elements and paintings. Built in the 19th century, the neo-Byzantine cathedral features art by prominent historical painters. The adjacent Austrian embassy was also damaged in the attack. UNESCO issued a condemnation, noting that historic structures within Odesa's World Heritage property, including the 1834 Kalio Palace, suffered damage. The strikes occurred amid heightened tensions following attacks on the Kerch Bridge, statements by Russian leadership rejecting partial ceasefires, and remarks by US President Donald Trump regarding peace efforts. Meanwhile, several European countries are seeking to bar Russia from participating in the 2027 Architecture Biennale.

articles.originalTitle: angelo renna’s eight principles for welcoming non-human life back into our cities - Designboom
articles.title: Eight Principles for Welcoming Non-Human Life into Urban Design
articles.excerpt: Designer Angelo Renna has published an eight-principle guide for integrating non-human species into urban environments. The recommendations focus on allowing spontaneous green growth, reducing lawn maintenance, and incorporating natural habitats.
articles.content: As human activities over the past half-century have contributed to a significant decline in global wildlife populations, designer Angelo Renna has outlined an eight-principle framework for integrating non-human species into urban environments. The guidelines advocate for allowing urban ecosystems to emerge naturally without excessive landscaping control, alongside reducing the frequency of intensive lawn mowing, which research links to decreased plant and invertebrate diversity. Additional principles include incorporating decaying tree trunks and snags to provide food and shelter for various organisms, providing water sources beyond simple drinking facilities for amphibians and insects, and utilizing porous construction materials and dry-stacked bricks to form microhabitats. The framework also emphasizes choosing diverse multispecies vegetation communities over monocultures to increase ecological resilience against environmental stress. Ultimately, the proposals envision the future city not merely as a human-centric development process, but as a shared habitat characterized by interspecific co-evolution and coexistence between humans and other forms of life.

articles.originalTitle: Conservation of the ‘Sistine Chapel of the Andes’ nears completion - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Conservation of the Sistine Chapel of the Andes Nears Completion
articles.excerpt: Conservation work at the Santiago de Curahuara de Carangas church in Bolivia, known for its extensive murals, is nearing completion following funding from a United States Department of State preservation fund.
articles.content: Conservation work at the Santiago de Curahuara de Carangas church in Bolivia, situated nearly 4,000 meters above sea level in the Andes, is nearing completion after beginning in May. Financed by the United States Department of State Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation, the project focused on the roofs, stone buttresses, and adobe walls of the historic structure, which was declared a National Monument in 1960. Project architect Josefina Matas noted that maintaining a sound roof is essential to protect the extensive interior murals from water leaks. The restoration team adopted local roof-building techniques, utilizing hollow cane brought from Tarija and layered straw. Road blockades during national protests in May and June delayed material deliveries, postponing completion by one month. Built by Augustinians between the late 16th and early 17th centuries, the church features murals depicting biblical scenes created with natural dyes and finished in 1777. The Bishop of Oruro, Krzysztof Białasik, submitted the project for funding. A celebratory mass is scheduled for December 15 with the bishop and the apostolic nuncio.

articles.originalTitle: In Sammy Baloji’s Hands, ‘Objective’ Materials Reveal New Truths About African History - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Sammy Baloji's Work Examines Colonial History and Mining Heritage Through Art
articles.excerpt: Artist Sammy Baloji explores the history of colonialism in the Democratic Republic of Congo, mining impacts, and European architectural legacies through photography, sculpture, and large-scale installations.
articles.content: Artist Sammy Baloji, who divides his time between Lubumbashi and Brussels, notes that his early work with researchers shaped his perspective on urban architecture and cultural heritage. Since his Mémoire project, which combined colonial archives with contemporary photographs, Baloji has investigated the social and political impacts of mining in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Baloji's debut US solo exhibition at the Wexner Center for the Arts runs through February 14, 2027, exploring how European decorative arts and architecture incorporate elements of Congo's colonial history. Concurrently, Baloji is showing sculptures and collage prints at the Venice Biennale's main exhibition and the national pavilion of the Democratic Republic of Congo. At the Wexner Center, he exhibits a suspended sculpture created from mining and construction waste. Born in 1978, Baloji cofounded the Picha Art and Research Center and the Lubumbashi Biennale in 2008, establishing platforms that support local artists and address extractivism and ecological crises.

articles.originalTitle: Poliform and Yabu Pushelberg brought a dreamlike design experience to Shanghai - Wallpaper*

articles.content: Italian furniture manufacturer Poliform and design studio Yabu Pushelberg presented their immersive installation Solstice at Shanghai's Yard 200 in November. Inspired by the cyclical rhythm of nature, the exhibition invited visitors to observe transitions between seasons through changing landscapes accessed via mirrored walls in an exterior garden. A winter-evoking room featured a mirrored glacier-like floor surrounding Aqualuna armchairs, while the main gallery introduced the Lanai bed system among green florals. Summer was represented by armchairs positioned on a reflective water surface, and a private VIP lounge brought autumn to life with earth-toned materials. This exhibition marked a continuation of the partnership between the Italian brand and the design studio following its introduction at Milan Design Week 2026. Poliform CEO Marco Spinelli noted that the Shanghai market is one of the most important and fast-growing for high-end design.

articles.originalTitle: Van Gogh’s record-breaking ‘Blossoming Chestnut Trees’: the $190m sale and the restitution claim that nearly upended it - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Van Gogh Painting Sells for $190.4 Million at Sotheby's Auction
articles.excerpt: Vincent van Gogh's 1890 work Blossoming Chestnut Trees sold for $190.4 million including fees at a Sotheby's New York auction, setting a new record for the artist.
articles.content: Vincent van Gogh's May 1890 painting Blossoming Chestnut Trees sold at Sotheby's New York for $190.4 million, including fees. Auctioneer Oliver Barker stated that the work was offered pursuant to an agreement between the seller and the heirs of the Hedwig and Samuel Fischer family. Opening at $135 million, the contest concluded in under four minutes with New York dealer William Acquavella placing the winning bid. Prior to the event, a potential Nazi-era restitution claim emerged regarding the 1936 transaction, but urgent negotiations led to a confidential settlement between the heirs and the Blaquier-Arrieta family, allowing the sale to proceed. While the Fischer family had sold the painting in 1936 following persecution due to their Jewish heritage, contemporary sales comparisons suggested they received a reasonable sum at the time. The final price marks a significant milestone, making it the fourth-highest price ever paid for an artwork at auction, surpassing the previous artist record set in 2022.

articles.originalTitle: Design Museum Gent / Carmody Groarke + ATAMA + RE-ST - ArchDaily
articles.title: Design Museum Gent Reopens Following Four Years of Intensive Renovation Work
articles.excerpt: Design Museum Gent has reopened its doors following four years of intensive transformation, featuring the restoration of listed buildings dating from the 16th to the 20th century alongside a new wing.
articles.content: Located close to UNESCO World Heritage sites, Design Museum Gent has opened its doors following four years of intensive restoration and expansion work. What was once a fragmented ensemble of buildings has been transformed into a forward-looking museum bringing together history, innovation, and sustainability. The transformation includes the restoration of listed buildings dating from the 16th through the 20th century. Furthermore, the addition of a striking new wing gives the institution a contemporary appearance. Designed collaboratively by architects ATAMA, Carmody Groarke, and RE-ST, the project was commissioned by the City of Ghent through sogent. Spanning 6500 square meters, the renewed museum features structural engineering by Ney & Partners and acoustic consulting by Daidalos Peutz. Project management was overseen by Brenda Schotte for sogent, with building services provided by Boydens Engineering.

articles.originalTitle: Connecting Old and New Through a Ceramic Facade - ArchDaily
articles.title: Martín Lejarraga Refurbishes Industrial Facility with Custom Ceramic Facade
articles.excerpt: Refurbishment and extension works at the HTBA industrial complex in Beniel feature a customized white ceramic facade developed by FAVEKER. Named Brooklyn and Sidney, the newly created three-dimensional ceramic pieces add architectural depth and a unified identity.
articles.content: Facilities for health technology and bioactive ingredient manufacturer HTBA in Beniel have been reorganized by Martín Lejarraga Oficina de Arquitectura while respecting the site's production logic. An office building and a changing-room pavilion near the entrance were unified under a shared architectural identity through a ceramic facade developed in collaboration with FAVEKER. To meet the project's technical requirements, two distinct three-dimensional extruded ceramic pieces were created: the concave Brooklyn and the convex Sidney. These components were subsequently added to FAVEKER's product catalog. The installation incorporates a total of 998.84 square meters of ceramic material, comprising 647.64 square meters on the office building and 351.20 square meters on the pavilion. Installed vertically using the FTS 505 system, the ceramic elements create continuous undulations across the facade. A red metal cornice positioned above the white ceramic surface introduces the company's corporate color and establishes a precise visual contrast.

articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a lunchtime lecture on the design of the Rosalinde and Arthur Gilbert Galleries, which reopened in March 2026. Alice Minter and Jessica Insley will share new narratives of the collection.
articles.content: V&A South Kensington in London is hosting a free lunchtime lecture focusing on the redesigned space of the Rosalinde and Arthur Gilbert Galleries, which reopened in March 2026. Taking place at the Lydia and Manfred Gorvy Lecture Theatre, the event examines the design processes of the galleries, which remain the only space at the museum dedicated to a private collection. articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul Exhibition Explores Sixteen Centuries of Art at V&A
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum presents Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition featuring over 200 objects that explore 1,600 years of artistic production across the Byzantine and Ottoman empires.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a comprehensive exhibition titled Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, which runs until 9 May 2027. The exhibition explores 1,600 years of artistic production spanning from AD 330 to 1922. It examines the enduring creative legacy of an imperial capital that shaped the Mediterranean world and beyond, highlighting the distinct yet connected traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires. The display showcases more than 200 objects across four main sections, featuring rare decorative arts, fine silks, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewellery, sculptures, manuscripts, and paintings. The exhibition is organized into four thematic sections: Roman Beginnings, Heaven and Earth, Power and Reach, and Life in the City. The opening section covers the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire, followed by sections exploring sacred imagery in Christianity, the visual spectacle of Ottoman court authority, and the cosmopolitan rhythms of urban life characterized by diverse languages and faiths. The exhibition concludes by tracing the influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century European culture.

articles.originalTitle: AOM Higher Education/Research: Utah State University Kem & Carolyn Gardner Learning & Leadership Building - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Utah State University Building Wins Recognition for Mass Timber Design
articles.excerpt: Utah State University's new academic facility, featuring a hybrid steel and mass timber system, received a regional project award.
articles.content: The Kem & Carolyn Gardner Learning & Leadership Building at Utah State University received an Award of Merit in the 2026 Mountain States Best Projects program. Located in Logan, the 44,658-sq-ft, three-story academic facility merges five academic centers from the Jon M. Huntsman School of Business under one roof. The structure represents the university's first mass timber building, utilizing a hybrid steel and mass timber system. Exposed glulam columns and cross-laminated timber decking realized a light-filled interior design inspired by nearby Logan Canyon. Jacobsen Construction served as the general contractor for the project, navigating a hemmed-in active construction site pressed against Highway 89. The mass timber structure supports the university's goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2040. The development team collaborated to conceal structural, mechanical, and electrical systems within cavities, preserving the visual continuity of the timber.

articles.originalTitle: Construction Starts on $246M Niagara Falls Power Station Hotel Conversion - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Historic Niagara Falls Power Station Converted Into Luxury Hotel
articles.excerpt: Construction has begun on a privately financed redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to convert the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station near Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex, with completion expected in 2029.
articles.content: Construction has commenced on a redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to transform the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station overlooking Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex. Owned by the Ontario provincial agency Niagara Parks, the historic facility is being redeveloped by Toronto Power Hotel Inc., a partnership overseeing the privately financed project. Deltera Contracting Inc. serves as the general contractor, with +VG Architects and MT Planners on the project team. Designed by E.J. Lennox, the steel-frame building opened in 1906 and operated until 1974. The preservation effort will maintain key architectural features while adding a five-star hotel, multiple restaurants, a wellness spa, event facilities, an art gallery, a museum, and public viewing areas. Audited financial statements indicate that approximately 6.72 million dollars in stabilization obligations were transferred to Society Land Holdings Inc. under a long-term lease. Substantial construction completion is anticipated in 2029, with the hotel opening scheduled for 2030.

articles.originalTitle: Building a Permanent Home for a Space Shuttle Was an Engineering Endeavor - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Los Angeles Unveils Permanent Home for Retired Space Shuttle Endeavour
articles.excerpt: The California Science Center has unveiled the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center in Los Angeles, a 450-million-dollar facility designed to permanently house the retired space shuttle Endeavour in launch position.
articles.content: The Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center at the California Science Center in Los Angeles has been formally unveiled. Completed at a cost of 450 million dollars and spanning 200,000 square feet, the facility provides a permanent home for the retired space shuttle Endeavour. Having flown its final mission in June 2011, Endeavour is the only space shuttle globally exhibited in the launch position. The 20-story exhibit comprises the orbiter, two solid rocket boosters, and an external tank. ZGF Architects, general contractor MATT Construction, and a team of engineers designed and built a 200-foot-tall curvilinear stainless-steel structure tailored to the shuttle stack's geometry. Project director Dennis R. Jenkins noted that seismic analysis was the most challenging aspect, requiring careful coordination to protect the fragile silica tiles of the shuttle, valued at 2 billion dollars by NASA. Arup provided comprehensive engineering services, while Plas-tal Manufacturing Co. fabricated the complex steel diagrid nodes. BrandSafway designed specialized scaffolding to safely guide components around the shuttle without contact.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach: Highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach 2026 Gathers the International Art World

articles.content: Situated at the cultural crossroads of the Americas, Art Basel Miami Beach prepares to unite the international art world from December 4 to 6, 2026. articles.originalTitle: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Birthday Exhibition at the Paris Mint - WWD
articles.title: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Exhibition at the Paris Mint
articles.excerpt: Grasse-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is opening a centenary exhibition featuring more than 250 works and objects at the Paris Mint.
articles.content: Frane-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is celebrating its centenary with a major exhibition at the Paris Mint. Entitled "Fragonard: 100 Years of Collections and Savoir-Faire," the event gathers more than 250 works and objects from the house's heritage collection. The exhibition remains open to the public through Jan. 17, 2027. Company chief executive officer Agnès Costa Webster noted that paintings from the family's collection in Grasse have been brought to Paris for the first time. Hosted at the 18th-century Hôtel de la Monnaie, the multisensory exhibition features paintings, perfume bottles, historic garments, silverware, and personal grooming accessories. Visitors can also explore an onsite boutique and attend fragrance-making workshops by reservation.

articles.originalTitle: Eight Dead, 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Eight Dead and 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Near Construction Site
articles.excerpt: An adjoining 96-year-old three-story building collapsed into an excavation site in Brooklyn, New York, leaving 8 people dead and 18 injured. Authorities have launched multiple investigations into the incident.
articles.content: On November 11, a three-story building collapsed into an adjoining excavation site in the Brooklyn borough of New York, resulting in 8 fatalities and 18 injuries. Officials confirmed the dead included two children and two construction workers, while the Fire Department concluded rescue operations on November 12. City records list Townhouse Builders as the general contractor for the project at 2625 Bedford Ave. A project geotechnical report had warned that abutting structures required underpinning and that construction-related vibrations could adversely affect neighboring properties. A March 5 preconstruction survey documented visible cracking at 1321 Flatbush Ave., rating its north masonry facade as poor and its other facades as fair. Area residents reported feeling heavy impacts and shaking while construction was underway next door. Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered safety inspections at approximately 100 other construction sites linked to companies involved in the project. New York Attorney General Letitia James stated that the Buildings Department would conduct a full investigation, alongside a separate probe launched by Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez. The exact cause of the structural collapse remains undetermined pending the conclusion of ongoing investigations by municipal authorities.

articles.originalTitle: Designers’ Creative Freedom Unveiled at Molteni Museum Exhibit - WWD
articles.title: Molteni Museum Exhibition Grants Designers Creative Freedom Away From Commerce
articles.excerpt: The new exhibition at the Molteni Museum in Giussano, Italy, offers prominent furniture designers the opportunity to reinterpret existing Molteni Group products without commercial and engineering constraints.
articles.content: Opening at the Molteni Compound in Giussano, Italy, a new exhibition provides creative figures in the furniture industry with a platform to produce one-off works free from commercial concerns. The collaborative showcase features creations by Ron Gilad, Herzog & de Meuron, Jean Nouvel, Naoto Fukasawa, OMA, AMDL Circle, Foster + Partners, Patricia Urquiola, the late Luca Meda, and Vincent Van Duysen. According to Ron Gilad, the initiative aimed to celebrate living creators rather than historical icons. Designers used existing items from the firm as starting points for experimental approaches. Herzog & de Meuron incorporated inflatable cushions into Porta Volta chairs, while OMA reinterpreted tables from the Principles collection in black and powder pink hues. AMDL Circle adapted the MDL System with unconventional contours. Molteni Group announced that the exhibition will remain on display for one year and is expected to travel to additional international cities.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | TAREK EL-ARISS | Emptying the Jars of War, or How We Learned to Love Nature - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Tarek El-Ariss to Discuss War, Nature, and Water Politics at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Tarek El-Ariss will examine how crises alter perceptions of nature and reframe sustainability during a lecture at Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Tarek El-Ariss is scheduled to speak at an event during Biennale Arte 2026 on November 21, 2026. Taking place at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale from 16:00 to 17:30, the lecture will be introduced and moderated by Rasha Salti. The session addresses how crises and wars not only damage the environment but also unsettle perceptions of nature. Drawing from everyday scenes such as saving water jars for bathing during wartime in Lebanon, the discussion traces longer histories and mythologies of water and greenery from the Garden of Eden to Greek and Islamic traditions, while focusing on the oasis as a recurring fantasy. The lecture posits that environmental practices do not necessarily emerge from ethical choices, often arising instead through habit, fear, or the quest for survival. Sustainability is reframed as a negotiation that interrogates the politics of purity and control to imagine alternative futures. Admission to the event is free until venue capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | LERATO SHADI | Unfolding - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Lerato Shadi's Performance Unfolding To Be Presented At Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Lerato Shadi's performance titled Unfolding, focusing on memory and collective processes, will meet audiences on November 21, 2026, within Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Shaped around memory, visibility, and collective processes, Unfolding is structured as a performance examining how meaning is produced and transmitted through bodies. The event will take place on November 21, 2026, from 12:00 to 12:40 in the Sala d’Armi E space. The work unfolds through a group relay structure where participants move to the stage, wrap a stone with red wool, and pass the transformed object to another participant. Through this repeated action, the object gradually changes form, accumulating time, touch, and traces of multiple hands. While wrapping becomes a gesture of protection and connection, passing the stone evokes histories and knowledge carried collectively rather than individually. Featuring Camille Badirou, Trovania Dellile, Viviana Medina, Rebecca Pokua Korang, and the artist herself, attendance requires a valid Biennale Arte 2026 admission ticket.

articles.originalTitle: Claude Monet | Waterlilies | L1406 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Claude Monet's 1905 Waterlilies Painting on Display in London
articles.excerpt: Claude Monet's 1905 painting Waterlilies forms part of his series inspired by his water gardens in Giverny. The artwork is housed at the National Gallery in London.
articles.content: After renting a house in Giverny west of Paris in 1883, Claude Monet eventually purchased the property and transformed the grounds into water gardens. Once the gardens matured, Monet turned to depicting them, making the water garden the subject of more than two hundred pictures. Between 1905 and 1908, he painted over sixty views of the pond exploring the contrast between tangible flowers and lily pads and the reflections of the unseen sky and overhanging trees. Housed at the National Gallery in London, Waterlilies exemplifies this series. In the painting, white flowers closest to the viewer feature purple accents for depth, while receding flowers are rendered in simple touches of white, yellow, pink, and red. The water itself consists of myriad tones of violets, blues, turquoise, and greens. The painting was included in Monet's 1909 exhibition at Durand-Ruel's gallery in Paris. Measuring 87 by 100 cm, the oil on canvas work is part of the Kenneth C. Griffin Collection.
